scenarios.name: Successful user registration with valid credentials
given: The email 'alice@example.com' is not already registered
when: User submits registration form with valid email and password
then: A new user account is created with status 'active'
Password is hashed using bcrypt before storage
User can immediately log in with the credentials

scenarios.name: Registration fails with weak password
given: The email 'bob@example.com' is not already registered
Password 'weak' does not meet complexity requirements
when: User attempts to register with weak password
then: User receives error message 'Password must be at least 8 characters and contain uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character'
Registration form remains displayed with email prefilled

scenarios.name: Account locks after 5 failed login attempts
given: User account 'charlie@example.com' exists and is active
Account has 4 failed login attempts within the last 15 minutes
when: User attempts login with incorrect password for the 5th time
then: User receives error message 'Account locked due to multiple failed attempts. Try again in 1 hour.'
Failed attempt is logged with timestamp and IP address

scenarios.name: Password reset link expires after 1 hour
given: User 'dana@example.com' requested password reset 61 minutes ago
Reset link was generated with 1-hour expiration
when: User clicks the password reset link
then: User sees error message 'Reset link has expired. Please request a new one.'
User is redirected to password reset request page

first_u_test.test_name: Password validation rejects passwords that don't meet complexity requirements
first_u_test.why_first: This is the First-U (highest priority) test based on complexity quadrant analysis
first_u_test.complexity_rationale: Password validation has multiple rules (length, uppercase, lowercase, number, special char) with various edge cases and boundary conditions
first_u_test.dependencies_rationale: Pure validation function with no external dependencies (no database, no network calls, no OAuth providers)
first_u_test.business_impact: Critical - prevents weak passwords, fundamental security requirement
first_u_test.risk_level: High - password security is foundational for entire authentication system
first_u_test.foundational_rationale: All other features (registration, login, password reset) depend on password validation working correctly
test_scenarios: Valid password with all required elements

tests.name: Password complexity validation
tests.rationale: Complex business rules, pure function, critical security requirement

tests.name: Failed login attempt tracking and account locking logic
tests.rationale: Stateful logic with time windows, edge cases (exactly 5 attempts, time boundary), critical for security

tests.name: Password reset token expiration validation
tests.rationale: Time-based logic with boundary conditions (exactly 1 hour), pure validation

quadrant_2_complex_many_deps.priority: Lowest - Test Last (or refactor to reduce dependencies)

tests.name: Complete OAuth flow with Google including redirects and callback
tests.rationale: Complex multi-step flow, depends on Google API, network calls, token exchange - better as integration test

tests.name: 2FA setup and verification complete workflow
tests.rationale: Multi-step process with TOTP library, QR code generation, database updates - integration test candidate

tests.name: Send password reset email via SendGrid
tests.rationale: Simple send operation but depends on external email service - focus on integration test with mocks

tests.name: Store user registration in PostgreSQL
tests.rationale: Simple CRUD operation with database dependency - integration test or repository layer test

tests.name: Email format validation
tests.rationale: Simple regex validation, pure function, quick win

tests.name: Password hashing with bcrypt produces different hash for same password
tests.rationale: Simple bcrypt library usage, deterministic with salt, pure function

testing_order_recommendation: 4. Failed login tracking and locking logic (Q1 - Critical)

issues: Creates user in real database (likely slow)
No indication of cleanup (may accumulate test data)
recommendations: Use in-memory database or mocks for unit tests
Measure execution time (should be < 100ms for unit test)

issues: Creates user in shared database (pollutes state)
No cleanup in test (affects subsequent tests)
Hardcoded email may conflict with other tests
recommendations: Each test should create and clean up its own data
Use unique test data (e.g., UUID in email)
Add teardown to remove created user

issues: May fail if 'test@example.com' already exists
No database reset between runs
recommendations: Generate unique email per test run
Reset database to known state in setup

issues: Doesn't verify password was hashed (security requirement)
Doesn't verify confirmation email was sent (requirement)
recommendations: Assert password in database is hashed, not plaintext
Verify email service was called with correct parameters

issues: Only tests happy path
Missing error cases (duplicate email, weak password, invalid email)
Missing edge cases (empty email, null password)
recommendations: Add test for duplicate email registration
Add test for password complexity validation failures
Add boundary tests (min password length, max email length)

issues: Test name is generic ('testUserRegistration')
Doesn't specify what specific behavior is being tested
recommendations: Rename to describe behavior: 'User registration succeeds with valid email and password'
Add docstring explaining the scenario

priority_fixes: P0: Add test isolation (create/cleanup own data)
P1: Verify all requirements (password hashing, email)

issues: Database query to fetch user (slow)
Depends on database state from another test
recommendations: Mock user retrieval
Create test user in this test's setup

issues: Critically broken: depends on user from previous test
Will fail if run in isolation
Execution order dependency
recommendations: CRITICAL: Each test must be independent
Create user in setup or test body
Don't rely on data from other tests

issues: Fails if testUserRegistration didn't run first
Fails if user data was modified by other tests
recommendations: Create known user state in test setup
Don't depend on test execution order

issues: Vague assertion: 'result == True' doesn't specify what 'result' represents
Doesn't verify session was created (core requirement)
Doesn't verify session token is valid
recommendations: Assert specific outcome: 'assert session.user_id == user.id'
Verify session token exists and is valid
Check session expiration is set correctly

issues: Only tests happy path
Missing: incorrect password test
Missing: non-existent user test
Missing: locked account test
recommendations: Test login failure with wrong password
Test login attempt on locked account
Test login with non-existent email

issues: Test name 'testLogin' is too generic
Variable 'result' is ambiguous
recommendations: Rename: 'User login succeeds with valid credentials and creates session'
Use descriptive variable: 'session' instead of 'result'

priority_fixes: P0: CRITICAL - Remove test interdependence (Isolated principle)
P0: Add error case tests (Thorough principle)

test_plan.summary: Test strategy for User Authentication System using FIRST-U methodology and complexity quadrant prioritization

p0_critical_tests.test: Password complexity validation rejects weak passwords
p0_critical_tests.rationale: Core security requirement, complex logic, no dependencies

p0_critical_tests.test: Account locks after 5 failed attempts within 15 minutes
p0_critical_tests.rationale: Critical security feature, stateful logic with time windows

p0_critical_tests.test: User registration succeeds with valid credentials

p1_important_tests.test: Password reset link expires after 1 hour
p1_important_tests.rationale: Time-based security feature, boundary conditions important

p1_important_tests.test: Email format validation rejects invalid emails

anti_patterns_to_avoid.why_bad: Violates Isolated principle, causes cascading failures
anti_patterns_to_avoid.fix: Each test creates and cleans up its own test data

anti_patterns_to_avoid.why_bad: Fragile tests that break with refactoring
anti_patterns_to_avoid.fix: Test behaviors and outcomes, not internal implementation

anti_patterns_to_avoid.why_bad: Violates Thorough principle, bugs hide in error cases
anti_patterns_to_avoid.fix: For each feature, test success + failure + edge cases

testing_order: 1. Write First-U Test: Password complexity validation (Q1)
2. Write Q4 Quick Wins: Email validation, password hashing verification
3. Write remaining Q1 tests: Failed login tracking, token expiration
4. Write Q3 integration tests: User registration, session creation
5. Write Q2 complex integrations: OAuth flow, 2FA workflow
6. Refactor existing broken tests to follow FIRST-U principles
7. Add missing error cases and edge cases for all features
